source_policy: SEER Cancer Stat Facts, ACS Cancer Facts & Figures 2026, USPSTF. Citable; refresh yearly. NCCN not used.

incidence.us_annual_new_cases: colorectal ~150,000+ annually; ~52,000+ deaths (ACS/SEER); colon-specific subset of colorectal
incidence.rank_among_cancers: colorectal is the 4th most common cancer and 2nd leading cause of cancer death
incidence.trend: Overall incidence falling ~0.5%/yr, but RISING in adults under 50 (early-onset CRC) — a key epidemiologic shift

mortality.trend: Mortality declining overall but rising in younger adults, mirroring the incidence shift

risk_factors.detail: Risk rises with age, though early-onset disease is increasing
Lynch syndrome (MMR), familial adenomatous polyposis (APC); strong family history
Long-standing ulcerative colitis or Crohn colitis
Processed/red meat, low fiber, obesity, physical inactivity, alcohol, smoking

screening.guideline_summary: USPSTF recommends screening for average-risk adults beginning at age 45 through 75 (individualized 76-85). Earlier for high-risk/hereditary. Cite USPSTF/ACS; NCCN not used.
screening.notes: Start age lowered to 45 in response to rising early-onset disease; colonoscopy both screens and removes precursor polyps

epidemiology.presentation: Change in bowel habits, rectal bleeding/blood in stool, abdominal discomfort, iron-deficiency anemia, or detected on screening before symptoms
